issue.title: test_app_import_budget fails: TUI app import loads 3576 modules against the 3570 cap after toobig splits and scope_sweep
issue.description:
`tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget`
fails on master f92bde8abe: `assert 3576 < 3570` (`_MAX_MODULE_COUNT = 3570`).

Found by the sase-1hi.10 land agent while auditing the epic. It is not caused by that
epic: none of the epic's modules are in the TUI import closure.

Bisected by importing `sase.ace.tui.app` from detached worktrees with the same venv
(`len(sys.modules)`):

- c929bb176b~1: 3566 (under the cap)
- 092fd1db05~1: 3574
- 9aa7ff2485: 3577
- master: 3576

The module-set diff names every added module. All come from mechanical toobig splits
and the scope-sweep feature:

- 24ccd12cd3 adds `sase.ace.tui._agent_completion_wait_{maps,models,queries}`
- e19b87ef94 adds `sase.ace.tui.actions.agents._wait_{apply,modal,relaunch,runner}`
- e4b0faf443 adds `sase.agent.scope_sweep`
- 9aa7ff2485 adds `sase.notification_gates.{adapter,adapter_plan,adapter_registry}`

The deferred-module probe still passes. Only the wholesale count guard trips.

Fix: re-measure the clean-tree closure. Then either keep the new split modules or
`scope_sweep` lazy on the TUI import path, or raise `_MAX_MODULE_COUNT` and extend the
growth comment above it, following the precedent in that comment. Never weaken the
deferred-module list.
